title: Delocalizing a smooth factorization over a localized base
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] ($A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_t)$), $\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra and $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. Let $S\subset R$ be a multiplicative subset, write $S^{-1}R$, $S^{-1}A$, $S^{-1}\Lambda$ for the localizations at $S$ (resp. at its images) [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and $S^{-1}\alpha:S^{-1}A\to S^{-1}\Lambda$, $a/u\mapsto\alpha(a)/u$, and let $S^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\beta'}B'\xrightarrow{\gamma'}S^{-1}\Lambda$ be homomorphisms of $S^{-1}R$-algebras with $\gamma'\circ\beta'=S^{-1}\alpha$ and $B'$ a smooth $S^{-1}R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then there are an $R$-algebra $B$ of finite presentation, homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $A\xrightarrow{\beta}B\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ with $\gamma\circ\beta=\alpha$, and an element $s\in S$ whose image in $B$ is elementary standard in $B$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F4 (lemma-delocalize-base, line 1937) and its proof (lines 1946-1997; the ring B constructed there is R[x_1,...,x_{n+m}]/(s'_1f_1,...,s'_cf_c,g_1,...,g_t), of finite presentation); uses Lemma lemma-smooth-standard-smooth and Lemma lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators

proof.text: (Reduction to $B'$ standard smooth.) By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-retract-standard-smooth] (Stacks 07CH) applied to the smooth $S^{-1}R$-algebra $B'$ there are a standard smooth $S^{-1}R$-algebra $B''$ [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra] and $S^{-1}R$-algebra maps $\iota:B'\to B''$, $\rho:B''\to B'$ with $\rho\circ\iota=\mathrm{id}_{B'}$. Then $S^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\iota\beta'}B''\xrightarrow{\gamma'\rho}S^{-1}\Lambda$ are $S^{-1}R$-algebra maps with $\gamma'\rho\iota\beta'=\gamma'\beta'=S^{-1}\alpha$. Replacing $(B',\beta',\gamma')$ by $(B'',\iota\beta',\gamma'\rho)$ we may assume that $B'$ is standard smooth over $S^{-1}R$; smoothness of $B'$ is not used again.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1947-1948 ('We first apply Lemma lemma-smooth-standard-smooth ... Thus we may assume B' is standard smooth')

proof.text: (Generators of $A$ and their images.) Fix a presentation $A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_t)$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], let $\bar x_i\in A$ be the class of $x_i$ and $\lambda_i=\alpha(\bar x_i)\in\Lambda$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. Since $\alpha$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, $g_j(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)=\alpha(g_j(\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_n))=\alpha(0)=0$ for $j=1,\dots,t$ (evaluation of polynomials commutes with $R$-algebra maps [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]). Moreover $A$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by $\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_n$, and $S^{-1}A$ is generated as an $S^{-1}R$-algebra by $\bar x_1/1,\dots,\bar x_n/1$, since $a/u=(1/u)\cdot(a/1)$ and $a$ is a polynomial in the $\bar x_i$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1949-1950 ('Write A = R[x_1..x_n]/(g_1..g_t) and say x_i -> lambda_i in Lambda')

proof.text: (A standard smooth presentation of $B'$ containing the generators of $A$.) Put $b_i=\beta'(\bar x_i/1)\in B'$, $i=1,\dots,n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-include-generators] (Stacks 07EY) applied to the standard smooth $S^{-1}R$-algebra $B'$ and $b_1,\dots,b_n$ there are $m\ge0$, $n\le c\le n+m$, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in P':=S^{-1}R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+m}]$ and an isomorphism $B'\cong P'/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ with $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}$ invertible in $B'$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] and the class of $x_i$ equal to $b_i$ for $i\le n$. Thus $\beta'$ is the $S^{-1}R$-algebra map with $\bar x_i/1\mapsto$ class of $x_i$ ($i\le n$), determined by these values by Step 2, and $\gamma'(\text{class of }x_i)=\gamma'\beta'(\bar x_i/1)=S^{-1}\alpha(\bar x_i/1)=\lambda_i/1$ for $i\le n$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1950-1954 ('We may write B' = S^{-1}R[x_1..x_{n+m}]/(f_1..f_c) for some c >= n ... A -> B' is given by x_i -> x_i, see Lemma lemma-standard-smooth-include-generators')

proof.text: (Rescaling the extra variables.) For $n<i\le n+m$ write $\gamma'(\text{class of }x_i)=\mu_i/u_i$ with $\mu_i\in\Lambda$, $u_i\in S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; put $u_i=1$ for $i\le n$. Let $\theta$ be the $S^{-1}R$-algebra automorphism of $P'$ with $\theta(x_i)=u_i^{-1}x_i$ (inverse $x_i\mapsto u_ix_i$) [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. It maps the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ onto $(\theta f_1,\dots,\theta f_c)$ and so induces $P'/(f)\cong P'/(\theta f)$, class of $u_ix_i\mapsto$ class of $x_i$. Composing, $B'\cong P'/(\theta f_1,\dots,\theta f_c)$ with the class of $x_i$ corresponding to $u_i$ times the old class of $x_i$; so for $i\le n$ nothing changes, and for $i>n$ the class of $x_i$ maps under $\gamma'$ to $u_i\mu_i/u_i=\mu_i/1$. By the formula for $\partial/\partial x_i$ on monomials [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative], $\partial(\theta f_j)/\partial x_i=u_i^{-1}\theta(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)$, so $\det(\partial\theta f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}=(\prod_{i\le c}u_i^{-1})\,\theta(\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c})$, which is a unit times the image of an invertible element, hence invertible in $B'$. Replacing $f_j$ by $\theta f_j$ we may assume that $\gamma'$ maps the class of $x_i$ to $\lambda_i/1$ with $\lambda_i\in\Lambda$ for all $i=1,\dots,n+m$ ($\lambda_i=\mu_i$ for $i>n$).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1955-1957 ('After multiplying x_i, i > n by an element of S and correspondingly modifying the equations f_j we may assume B' -> S^{-1}Lambda maps x_i to lambda_i/1')

proof.text: ($P'$ is the localization of $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+m}]$ at $S$.) Let $\varphi:P\to P'$ be the map applying $R\to S^{-1}R$ to the coefficients. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] $P'\cong S^{-1}R\otimes_RP$ compatibly with $\varphi$ ($p\mapsto1\otimes p$), and by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] (with $D=P$ and $R\to S^{-1}R$ the localization at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]) $P\to P\otimes_RS^{-1}R$ is a localization of $P$ at the image of $S$. Hence: (a) every element of $P'$ is $u^{-1}\varphi(p)$ with $p\in P$, $u\in S$, and finitely many elements have a common denominator (the product of the denominators); (b) $\varphi(p)=\varphi(q)$ implies $vp=vq$ for some $v\in S$; (c) every $u\in S$ is a unit in $P'$. Moreover (d) $\varphi$ commutes with each $\partial/\partial x_i$ (both sides are computed coefficientwise by the monomial formula [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]) and hence with Jacobian determinants.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1964-1965 ('Since each element of S is invertible in B' we may (by clearing denominators) ...'): the localization facts used there

proof.text: (Clearing the denominators of the $f_j$.) By Step 5(a) write $f_j=u_j^{-1}\varphi(p_j)$ with $p_j\in P$, $u_j\in S$. Since $u_j$ is a unit of $P'$ (Step 5(c)), replacing $f_j$ by $u_jf_j=\varphi(p_j)$ changes neither the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ nor the classes of the $x_i$, hence neither the isomorphism with $B'$ nor $\beta',\gamma'$, and it multiplies $\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}$ by the unit $u_1\cdots u_c$ ($\partial/\partial x_i$ is $S^{-1}R$-linear and the determinant is linear in each row [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]), so it stays invertible in $B'$. Hence we may assume $f_j=\varphi(f_j^0)$ with $f_j^0\in P$; we write $f_j$ for $f_j^0\in P$ from now on, and $\Delta=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j=1,\dots,c}\in P$, so that $\varphi(\Delta)$ is the Jacobian determinant of the $\varphi(f_j)$ (Step 5(d)) and is invertible in $B'=P'/(\varphi(f_1),\dots,\varphi(f_c))$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1964-1966 ('we may (by clearing denominators) assume that f_j, a_j in R[x_1..x_{n+m}]')

proof.text: (The relation with $s_0$.) Since $\varphi(\Delta)$ is invertible in $B'=P'/(\varphi(f))$ there is $a'_0\in P'$ with $a'_0\varphi(\Delta)-1\in(\varphi(f_1),\dots,\varphi(f_c))$, i.e. $1=a'_0\varphi(\Delta)+\sum_{j=1}^ca'_j\varphi(f_j)$ for some $a'_j\in P'$. By Step 5(a) write $a'_j=u^{-1}\varphi(a''_j)$ ($j=0,\dots,c$) with $a''_j\in P$ and one $u\in S$; multiplying by $u$ gives $\varphi(u)=\varphi(a''_0\Delta+\sum_ja''_jf_j)$, so by Step 5(b) $v(u-a''_0\Delta-\sum_ja''_jf_j)=0$ in $P$ for some $v\in S$. With $s_0=vu\in S$ and $a_j=va''_j\in P$: $s_0=a_0\Delta+\sum_{j=1}^ca_jf_j$ in $P$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1957-1971 (choice of the relation 1 = a_0 det + sum a_j f_j and its version s_0 = a_0 det + sum a_j f_j over R)

proof.text: (The elements $s_j$, $j=1,\dots,t$.) The image of $\varphi(g_j)$ ($g_j\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\subset P$) in $B'$ is $g_j$ evaluated at the classes of $x_1,\dots,x_n$, which is $\beta'(g_j(\bar x_1,\dots,\bar x_n)/1)=\beta'(0)=0$ by Step 3 ($\beta'$ is an $S^{-1}R$-algebra map sending $\bar x_i/1$ to the class of $x_i$) [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. So $\varphi(g_j)=\sum_kh_k\varphi(f_k)$ with $h_k\in P'$; writing $h_k=u^{-1}\varphi(h'_k)$ (Step 5(a)) gives $\varphi(ug_j)=\varphi(\sum_kh'_kf_k)$, so $v(ug_j-\sum_kh'_kf_k)=0$ for some $v\in S$ (Step 5(b)). With $s_j=vu\in S$: $s_jg_j\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)P$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1972-1974 ('Since g_j maps to zero in S^{-1}R[x]/(f) we can find s_j in S such that s_j g_j = 0 in R[x]/(f_1..f_c)')

proof.text: (The elements $s'_j$, $j=1,\dots,c$.) The $R$-algebra maps $P\xrightarrow{\varphi}P'\to B'\xrightarrow{\gamma'}S^{-1}\Lambda$ and $P\to\Lambda\to S^{-1}\Lambda$ (evaluation at $(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{n+m})$, then $\lambda\mapsto\lambda/1$) agree on every $x_i$ by Steps 3 and 4, hence are equal [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Since $\varphi(f_j)$ maps to $0$ in $B'$, $f_j(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{n+m})/1=0$ in $S^{-1}\Lambda$, so there is $s'_j\in S$ with $s'_jf_j(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{n+m})=0$ in $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1975-1977 ('Since f_j maps to zero in S^{-1}Lambda we can find s'_j in S such that s'_j f_j(lambda) = 0')

proof.text: (The factorization.) Let $B=P/(s'_1f_1,\dots,s'_cf_c,g_1,\dots,g_t)$, an $R$-algebra of finite presentation ($n+m$ variables, $c+t$ relations) [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. The $R$-algebra map $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to B$, $x_i\mapsto$ class of $x_i$, kills each $g_j$, so it induces $\beta:A\to B$, $\bar x_i\mapsto$ class of $x_i$. The evaluation $P\to\Lambda$, $x_i\mapsto\lambda_i$, kills $s'_jf_j$ (Step 9) and $g_j$ (Step 2), so it induces $\gamma:B\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. The $R$-algebra maps $\gamma\beta$ and $\alpha$ agree on the generators $\bar x_i$ of $A$ ($\gamma\beta(\bar x_i)=\lambda_i=\alpha(\bar x_i)$), so $\gamma\circ\beta=\alpha$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1978-1982 ('Consider the ring B = R[x_1..x_{n+m}]/(s'_1f_1..s'_cf_c,g_1..g_t) and the factorization A -> B -> Lambda with B -> Lambda given by x_i -> lambda_i')

proof.text:
($s$ is elementary standard in $B$ over $R$.) Let $s=s_0s_1\cdots s_ts'_1\cdots s'_c\in S$. Use the presentation of Step 10 with relations $F_j=s'_jf_j$ ($j\le c$), $F_{c+j}=g_j$ ($j\le t$) and the integer $c$; $0\le c\le\min(n+m,c+t)$ since $c\le n+m$ (Step 3). Second condition of [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element](1), lifting the image of $s$ to $s\in R\subset P$: by Step 8, $s_jg_j=\sum_kh_kf_k$ with $h_k\in P$, so $sg_j= igl(s_0\prod_{l
e j}s_l igr)\sum_kh_k igl(\prod_{l
e k}s'_l igr)F_k\in(F_1,\dots,F_c)\subset(F_1,\dots,F_c)+(F_1,\dots,F_{c+t})^2$. First condition: $\partial F_j/\partial x_i=s'_j\,\partial f_j/\partial x_i$ ($R$-linearity of $\partial/\partial x_i$ [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]), so $\det(\partial F_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}=s'_1\cdots s'_c\Delta$ by multilinearity in the rows. Multiplying the relation of Step 7 by $s'_1\cdots s'_c$ gives $a_0\det(\partial F_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}+\sum_{j=1}^c igl(\prod_{l
e j}s'_l igr)a_jF_j=s_0s'_1\cdots s'_c$ in $P$. In $B$ all $F_j$ vanish, so $s_0s'_1\cdots s'_c=a_0\det(\partial F_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}$ and $s=a'\det(\partial F_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\le c}$ in $B$ with $a'$ the image of $s_1\cdots s_ta_0$. Hence the image of $s$ in $B$ is elementary standard in $B$ over $R$, which with Step 10 proves the lemma.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F4, lines 1983-1997 ('We claim that s = s_0 s_1...s_t s'_1...s'_c is elementary standard ... s_j g_j in (f) and hence s g_j in (s'_1f_1..s'_cf_c) ... a_0 det(d s'_j f_j/dx_i) + sum (s'_1..^s'_j..s'_c) a_j s'_j f_j = s_0 s'_1...s'_c which divides s')

split_report.summary: Proof written in 11 steps following the Stacks proof of 07F4 line by line: reduction to B' standard smooth via 07CH (which gives a standard smooth B'' with a retraction onto B', not a localization: the factorization is rerouted through B'' and the retraction); presentation of A and the lambda_i; standard smooth presentation of B' containing the images of the generators of A (07EY); the rescaling of the extra variables by elements of S, written out with the Jacobian (Stacks one sentence); the localization facts for R[x] -> S^{-1}R[x] (polynomial-scalar-extension + localization-base-change leaves); clearing denominators of f_j and a_j (relation s_0 = a_0 Delta + sum a_j f_j); s_j for the g_j, s'_j for the f_j(lambda); B, beta, gamma; the verification of both conditions of 'elementary standard' (Definition 07C7 (1), as in the statement; not 'strictly standard') with a' = s_1...s_t a_0. Statement: unchanged in content; S^{-1}A, S^{-1}Lambda, S^{-1}alpha spelled out and stmt_deps gained def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra and def-weil-pbc-module-localization. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-smooth-retract-standard-smooth (07CH), lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-include-generators (07EY, stated for a family a_1..a_n as the proof allows). Stacks typo '(f_1, ..., x_c)' at line 1973 read as (f_1,...,f_c).

reviewed.note: 11 steps follow Stacks 07F4 line by line: reduction to B' standard smooth via a retraction (new 07CH node), a standard smooth presentation containing the generators of A (new 07EY node, stated for a family), rescaling and clearing denominators (polynomial scalar extension and localization base change leaves), the relations with s_0, s_j, s'_j, the algebra B and the factorization, and the check of 'elementary standard' against the definition (with the Jacobian det(F) = prod s'_j Delta). Statement made explicit (S^{-1}A etc.). Tags 07F4, 07CH, 07EY, 07C7 verified.
